tables.title: Maximum path lengths, per-layer complexity and minimum number of sequential operations for different layer types. $n$ is the sequence length, $d$ is the representation dimension, $k$ is the kernel size of convolutions and $r$ the size of the neighborhood in restricted self-attention.
notes: In the text: 'As noted in Table 1, a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires $O(n)$ sequential operations.'
The table caption defines variables: $n$ = sequence length, $d$ = representation dimension, $k$ = kernel size of convolutions, $r$ = size of neighborhood in restricted self-attention.

observations: Section 3.5 discusses positional encoding using sine/cosine functions with formulas: $PE_{(pos,2i)} = sin(pos/10000^{2i/d_{model}})$ and $PE_{(pos,2i+1)} = cos(pos/10000^{2i/d_{model}})$.
Section 4 introduces comparison criteria: total computational complexity per layer, amount of parallelizable computation (min sequential operations), and path length between long-range dependencies.
The text states that self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence is long, per Table 1 computational complexity.
uncertainties: The exact value of $d_{model}$ is not specified in the excerpt; it appears only in the positional encoding formulas.
The phrase 'see Table 3 row (E)' refers to an external table not present on page 6.
The term 'restricted self-attention' is used without explicit definition beyond the note about neighborhood size $r$.
